notes: Read against the maker's source at commit 96f186f, "Code cleanup. Release 2.0.3.", which is the last commit whose plugin.json carries the installed version 2.0.3; the next commit bumps it to 2.0.4. The README at that commit is the only manual. Eleven of the sixteen modules carry MIDI on ordinary patch cables under the maker's vMIDI scheme: a three-byte message is packed into a 24-bit integer and written to the jack as that integer negated, so the voltage is zero or large and negative and carries no signal meaning at all (utils/CVMidi.h:68-145). None of those jacks is given a family, because none of audio, cv, trigger or pitch describes what a cable into one carries, and a colour that says "patch a gate here" would be a lie. They are all one channel. RT_TASK_RATE is 4000 in plugin.hpp:54, so every timeout quoted in task runs has been divided by 4000 to get the seconds in the lines; two of the maker's own comments give the wrong figure and are listed on the modules concerned.

MIDI_CV.notes: Pitch is note times one twelfth minus 5V plus the bend, at Midi2Note/Midi2Note.cpp:291, so note 60 sits at 0V. The smoothing constants are PITCH_GATE_SMOOTHING and CC_CV_SMOOTHING at plugin.hpp:52-53. BEND_RANGE is a tenth parameter with no configParam and no widget; it exists only to save the menu choice into the patch.

Quad_Panner.notes: The pan law is at Quad_Panner.cpp:108-115: the axis position is mapped to 0 to 1 and each side takes the arc tangent of that times 1.7, clamped to positive. The joystick is a KilpatrickJoystick widget added at :195 with no ParamWidget behind it, so only RESET appears in the census paramPos. lines: A MIDI clock running at 24 pulses per quarter note, generating its own tempo or following an analogue or MIDI clock, with analogue and vMIDI outputs
Sends the clock back to the start of the count, pulses RESET OUT, and sends a song position of zero out of MIDI OUT
Starts the clock if it is stopped and stops it if it is running, sending the matching MIDI start, continue or stop message
Runs and stops the clock; how the voltage here is read is set by Run In Mode on the menu, and the lamp beside the jack tracks the voltage
A rising edge above 1V stops the clock, whatever the RUN IN jack is doing
Takes an analogue clock at 24 pulses per quarter note, counting a tick on each rising edge above 1V; for 2 seconds after each edge it overrides the clock arriving at MIDI IN
A rising edge above 1V resets the clock count and pulses RESET OUT, and for 2 seconds afterwards it overrides the clock arriving at MIDI IN
Takes a vMIDI stream and follows its timing ticks, start, continue and stop; a recent edge on CLOCK IN or RESET IN takes precedence over it
Carries timing ticks at 24 per quarter note the whole time, running or stopped, with start, continue, stop and song position sent as they happen
A 4ms pulse to 10V on every tick that survives the output divider, and only while the clock is running
A 4ms pulse to 10V whenever the clock count is reset, from the button, the RESET IN jack or a MIDI start
Note — the tempo, the run state, the clock source, the output divider and the autostart setting are all on the black display, and none of them can be clicked for help
Note — scroll over the large number on the display to change the tempo a beat per minute at a time, 30 to 300; hold shift while scrolling to move it by 0.1, and click the number to tap a tempo
Note — click the word INT or EXT on the display to switch between the module's own tempo and following an incoming clock; EXT is drawn cyan while it is locked and red while it is not
Note — click the word RUN or STOP on the display to start and stop the clock
Note — scroll over the d:1/ reading on the display to divide the CLOCK OUT jack, from 1/1, which is every tick, down to 1/24, which is one pulse per quarter note
Note — click the word MAN or AUTO on the display to switch autostart; with AUTO showing, the clock starts on its own a fraction of a second after a patch is loaded
Menu — Run In Mode: Momentary, Run, Toggle — sets how the RUN IN jack is read; Momentary runs while it is high, Run starts on a high but never stops, Toggle flips the run state on each rising edge

lines: Turns MIDI controller messages into note messages, one note per controller number, for playing from the buttons on a controller
Scales the velocity of the notes sent; the controller's own value is multiplied by this, so at full clockwise a value of 127 gives velocity 127 and at halfway it gives 63
Moves the notes up one octave for each press, as far as six octaves above normal
Puts the notes back to no octave shift
Moves the notes down one octave for each press, as far as six octaves below normal
Takes the vMIDI stream whose controller messages become notes; every controller value is converted, despite the manual saying a value below 64 is read as a release
Carries the notes made from the controllers, always on channel 1; nothing else from the input reaches it
Note — the note number is the controller number, plus the CC Base setting, plus twelve times the octave shift; a note landing outside 0 to 127 is not sent at all
Note — only controller messages are converted; notes, clock and everything else arriving at the input are dropped
Note — a controller repeating the value it last sent, within 2 seconds, is ignored, so a control that sends continuously does not flood the output
Note — every message sent is a note on, and a controller value of 0 gives velocity 0, which is how a note is released
Note — the display reads T: and the octave shift, and switches to N: and the last note number for a moment after each note
Menu — CC Base: 0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120 — added to every controller number before it becomes a note, so it sets which note controller 0 produces

MIDI_CC_Note.notes: The README says the controller value must be 64 or more for a press and below 64 for a release. No such threshold is in the code: MIDI_CC_Note.cpp:165-176 turns every controller message that survives the repeat filter into a note on, with the velocity taken from the controller value scaled by the VELOCITY knob, so a value of 0 arrives as a note on at velocity 0, which is the MIDI convention for a release. The effect is close to what the README describes but the boundary is 0, not 64. The README also says the CC Base setting shifts events to start at note 60; that is true only of the 60 choice. The output channel is fixed: encodeNoteOnMessage is called with channel 0 at :172 and utils/MidiHelper.cpp:578 puts that in the low nibble, which is MIDI channel 1. The octave clamp is OCT_OFFSET_MIN and OCT_OFFSET_MAX, -6 to +6, at :55-56. The repeat filter is a MidiRepeater fixed at MODE_OFF at :83, with the 2-second history timeout from utils/MidiRepeater.h:46. Two parameters, OCT_OFFSET and CC_BASE, have no widget; they hold the octave shift and the menu choice. The panel prints OCT NORM where the parameter is named OCT NORMAL.
